# Xenon

**Authors:** Tushar Bajaj, Marco Cascella, Judith Borger

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Xenon is an element with the symbol Xe, has an atomic number 54, and belongs to group 18 of the periodic table. Xe is a monoatomic, inert gas, first discovered in 1898 by British chemists William Ramsay (1852-1916) and Morris Travers (1872-1961) in the residue left after partial evaporation of liquid air (with krypton as an impurity). Xe is a colorless, odorless, non-pungent, nontoxic, nonexplosive, and environmentally friendly noble gas. Xe exists in trace amounts in the Earth's atmosphere, with a concentration of only 0.086 ppm, and is also found in gases emitted from certain mineral springs. The name Xe is derived from the Greek word for "stranger," which reflects its rarity. Of its 9 naturally occurring isotopes, Xe-132 is the most abundant.
